items.code:
import os.path

def user_file(base, name):
    path = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, name))
    if not path.startswith(base + os.sep):
        raise ValueError("path escapes base")
    return path

print(user_file("/srv/uploads", "report.txt"))

clean-js-sort-comparator
items.verified: by inspection: `(a, b) => a - b` sorts [2, 9, 10, 100]; the copy has the same length as xs, so index xs.length - 1 is the last element, 100. The caller's array is untouched because sort runs on the spread copy.
items.why_correct: the comparator makes the sort numeric and the spread sorts a copy, so neither the string-ordering trap nor the in-place mutation of the caller's array applies

items.name: buggy-au-t1-w102c0-py-max-cheapest-vendor
items.code:
quotes = {"acme": 340, "bolt": 295, "crane": 410}
budget = 350
best_vendor = max(quotes, key=quotes.get)
cost = quotes[best_vendor]
print("cheapest:", best_vendor, cost)
print("within budget:", cost <= budget)
items.verified: exec: exit 0; stdout = 'cheapest: crane 410 | within budget: False'
items.cause: max picks the highest quote, so it reports crane 410 and False instead of bolt 295 and True
items.source: authored (claude-opus-5-5) for olmo-3-7b: About 8 lines of Python. A single-step VALUE bug a careful reader traces in one pass: a wrong operator (- for +), an inverted comparison, an accumulator reset inside the loop, integer division where a fraction is needed, a wrong variable returned. Small literal inputs, so the output is easy to compute by hand.

bids = {"ana": 120, "raj": 175, "lin": 140}
reserve = 150
top_bidder = max(bids, key=bids.get)
amount = bids[top_bidder]
print("winner:", top_bidder, amount)
print("meets reserve:", amount >= reserve)
items.verified: exec: exit 0; stdout = 'winner: raj 175 | meets reserve: True'
items.why_correct: the auction winner is the highest bid, so max correctly gives raj 175 and True
